extracted.intended_audience: sovereigns, ministers, theologians, and learned readers of political theology
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of principles for a Christian commonwealth: the authority and interpretation of Scripture, signs of prophecy, the relation of natural reason to revelation, and the sovereign's role in making religious books law. Targets how rulers and subjects should treat prophecy, miracles, canon, and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science necessary for sovereigns
rubrics_metrics.description: The Science of Naturall Justice, is the onely Science necessary for Soveraigns, and their principall Ministers; and that they need not be charged with the Sciences Mathematicall, (as by Plato they are,) further, than by good Lawes to encourage men to the study of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sovereigns should concern themselves principally with natural justice and its practical application; they may encourage mathematical and other studies by law but need not be experts. The aim is to produce clear, practicable guidance for government rather than exhaustive philosophical proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use natural reason alongside revelation
rubrics_metrics.description: We are not to renounce our Senses, and Experience; nor (that which is the undoubted Word of God) our naturall Reason. For they are the talents which he hath put into our hands ... therefore not to be folded up in the Napkin of an Implicate Faith, but employed in the purchase of Justice, Peace, and true Religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scripture and prophetic revelation must be interpreted and applied using senses, experience, and natural reason; nothing in God's Word is contrary to reason, and apparent contradictions owe to bad interpretation or faulty reasoning. Use reason to deduce rules and precepts necessary for duty to God and man.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captivity of the understanding (obedience distinguished from assent)
rubrics_metrics.description: By the Captivity of our Understanding, is not meant a Submission of the Intellectual faculty, to the Opinion of any other man; but of the Will to Obedience, where obedience is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captivating the understanding means forbearing contradiction, speaking as lawfully commanded, and living accordingly — i.e., outward trust and obedience to lawful authority even when the mind lacks understanding. It does not require intellectual assent to another's opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility of private revelations
rubrics_metrics.description: When God speaketh to man, it must be either immediately; or by mediation of another man ... To say he hath spoken to him in a Dream, is no more than to say he dreamed that God spake to him ... To say he speaks by supernaturall Inspiration, is to say he finds an ardent desire to speak ... yet he obliges no man to beleeve he hath so done to him that pretends it; who (being a man), may erre, and (which is more) may lie.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of immediate or private revelation (dreams, visions, inspirations) do not obligate others to belief or obedience unless the claimant possesses legitimate sovereign authority. Such claims are often natural (dreams) or products of self-conceit and can be false or deceitful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marks of a true prophet
rubrics_metrics.description: There be two marks, by which together, not asunder, a true Prophet is to be known. One is the doing of miracles; the other is the not teaching any other Religion than that which is already established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither miracles nor doctrinal conformity alone is sufficient to prove immediate revelation; both must co-occur. Miracles performed in favour of doctrines that promote revolt against the sovereign are to be treated as tests of allegiance (and disallowed). False prophets may perform miracles; teaching that contradicts established religion invalidates the prophet regardless of miraculous signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that prophetic miracles be confirmed by near-term events
rubrics_metrics.description: The miracles that oblige us to beleeve a Prophet, ought to be confirmed by an immediate, or a not long deferr’d event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predictions or miracles purported to confirm prophecy must be followed by proximate, verifiable events; distant or indefinitely-timed prophecies do not furnish useful proof and therefore are insufficient to establish prophetic authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scripture supplies the place of prophecy when miracles cease
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeing therefore Miracles now cease, we have no sign left, whereby to acknowledge the pretended Revelations, or Inspirations of any private man; nor obligation to give ear to any Doctrine, farther than it is conformable to the Holy Scriptures, which since the time of our Saviour, supply the want of all other Prophecy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since miraculous confirmation of prophets has ceased, the standard for accepting doctrine is conformity to Holy Scripture; private revelations are to be judged by their agreement with Scripture and by careful, rational interpretation (avoiding enthusiasm).

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonicity determined by sovereign or church authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Those Books only are Canonicall, that is, Law, in every nation, which are established for such by the Soveraign Authority. ... I can acknowledge no other Books of the Old Testament, to be Holy Scripture, but those which have been commanded to be acknowledged for such, by the Authority of the Church of England.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canonical status is not primarily a matter of authorship or antiquity but of being established by legitimate authority (the sovereign or the church recognized by the sovereign). Historical notes (e.g., Septuagint, Jerome, councils) inform but do not alone determine canonicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scripture's authority as law depends on conformity to natural law or legislative recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: As far as they differ not from the Laws of Nature, there is no doubt, but they are the Law of God ... If they be made Law by God himselfe, they are of the nature of written Law, which are Laws to them only to whom God hath so sufficiently published them ... He therefore, to whom God hath not supernaturally revealed, that they are his, ... is not obliged to obey them, by any Authority, but his, whose Commands have already the force of Laws; that is to say, by any other Authority, then that of the Common-wealth, residing in the Soveraign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scripture carries binding moral authority where it aligns with natural law; where it claims legislative force beyond natural law, its obligation for subjects depends on either divine revelation (which is not universal) or the positive recognition of the sovereign/commonwealth or church. Without such public authority, individuals are not generally bound by scripture as law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive authority follows legislative power
rubrics_metrics.description: Whosoever hath a lawfull power over any Writing, to make it Law, hath the power also to approve, or disapprove the interpretation of the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The person or body that lawfully makes a writing into law (the sovereign or constituted church authority) also has the legitimate authority to determine its official interpretation. Interpretive power is therefore political as well as hermeneutical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define ambiguous terms from Scripture before reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation of all true Ratiocination, is the constant Signification of words; ... It is necessary, before I proceed any further, to determine, out of the Bible, the meaning of such words, as by their ambiguity, may render what I am to inferre upon them, obscure, or disputable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before making inferences from Scripture, fix clear, scripturally-grounded definitions for ambiguous terms (examples given: BODY and SPIRIT). Precise signification of words is essential to sound reasoning and to avoid dispute or obscurity.
